questions.knowledge_point: Adding and Subtracting Rational Expressions With No Common Factors in the Denominators
questions.worked_solution:
In this case, we need to put the fractions over a common denominator of $z(z-3),$ since there are no common factors in either denominator that we can exploit.

To do this, we multiply the top and bottom of the first fraction by $z-3$, and the top and bottom of the second fraction by $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{z}+\frac{3}{z-3} & = \\ \frac{z-3}{z-3}\cdot \frac{1}{z}+\frac{z}{z}\cdot \frac{3}{z-3} & = \\ \frac{z-3}{z(z-3)}+\frac{3z}{z(z-3)} & = \\ \frac{z-3+3z}{z(z-3)} & = \\ \frac{4z-3}{z(z-3)} & \end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
In this case, we need to put the fractions over a common denominator of $x(2x-1),$ since there are no common factors in either denominator that we can exploit. 

To do this, we multiply the top and bottom of the first fraction by $x,$ and the top and bottom of the second fraction by $2x-1:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6}{2x-1}-\frac{3}{x} & = \\ \frac{x}{x}\cdot \frac{6}{2x-1}-\frac{2x-1}{2x-1}\cdot \frac{3}{x} & = \\ \frac{6x}{x(2x-1)}-\frac{3(2x-1)}{x(2x-1)} & = \\ \frac{6x-3(2x-1)}{x(2x-1)} & = \\ \frac{6x-6x+3}{x(2x-1)} & = \\ \frac{3}{x(2x-1)}\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, we need to put the fractions over a common denominator of $(x-6)(2x+3),$ since there are no common factors in either denominator that we can exploit. 

To do this, we multiply the top and bottom of the first fraction by $2x+3,$ and the top and bottom of the second fraction by $x-6:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4y}{x-6}+\frac{2y}{2x+3} & = \\ \frac{2x+3}{2x+3}\cdot \frac{4y}{x-6}+\frac{x-6}{x-6}\cdot \frac{2y}{2x+3} & = \\ \frac{4y(2x+3)}{(x-6)(2x+3)}+\frac{2y(x-6)}{(x-6)(2x+3)} & = \\ \frac{4y(2x+3)+2y(x-6)}{(x-6)(2x+3)} & = \\ \frac{8xy+12y+2xy-12y}{(x-6)(2x+3)} & = \\ \frac{10xy}{(x-6)(2x+3)}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Adding and Subtracting a Number and a Rational Expression
questions.worked_solution:
Using the fact that $5=\frac{5}{1},$ we can write the expression as

$$
\frac{5}{1}+\frac{h-3}{h}.
$$

 

In order to add the two fractions, we need them to have a common denominator. So, we put both fractions over a common denominator of $h$ by multiplying the top and bottom of the first fraction by $h:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{1}+\frac{h-3}{h} & = \\ \frac{h}{h}\cdot \frac{5}{1}+\frac{h-3}{h} & = \\ \frac{5h}{h}+\frac{h-3}{h}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we add the fractions and simplify the result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5h}{h}+\frac{h-3}{h} & = \\ \frac{5h+h-3}{h} & = \\ \frac{6h-3}{h} & = \\ \frac{3(2h-1)}{h}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Adding and Subtracting a Number and a Rational Expression
questions.worked_solution:
Using the fact that $6=\frac{6}{1},$ we can write the expression as

$$
\frac{6}{1}+\frac{3-2k}{k}.
$$

 

In order to add the two fractions, we need them to have a common denominator. So, we put both fractions over a common denominator of $k$ by multiplying the top and bottom of the first fraction by $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6}{1}+\frac{3-2k}{k} & = \\ \frac{k}{k}\cdot \frac{6}{1}+\frac{3-2k}{k} & = \\ \frac{6k}{k}+\frac{3-2k}{k}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we add the fractions and simplify the result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6k}{k}+\frac{3-2k}{k} & = \\ \frac{6k+3-2k}{k} & = \\ \frac{4k+3}{k}\end{aligned}
$$
